findings.detail: The changelog says an aligned demanded boundary is now captured "below the normal solo stripe, so repeated short prefixes can be published for reuse". It also says repeated checkpoints get the reserved SSD write share on first local appearance. T-041 records the encrypted SSD tier as signed off only for donations whose whole-block prefix exceeds the model's adoption bound plus the 1,024-token benefit floor. T-041's detection_hint says loosening that gate widens the at-rest surface and needs a fresh SEC-035 review. If this code lets sub-threshold prefixes reach SSDPrefixCache.donate, more at-rest artifacts are written and the same-account TTFT oracle extends to short prefixes. Only the changelog was supplied, so the actual gate behaviour is unverified. Fix: confirm that the SSD donation guard still applies to demanded short captures, or document the exception and refresh the T-041/SEC-035 sign-off.
findings.title: Changelog describes publishing short repeated prefixes to the SSD cache, outside the T-041 per-donation gate
